candidates.title: Self-Verifying Handoff with Provenance Hashing
candidates.uncertainty: Whether the instrument’s hardware or software can support lightweight cryptographic hashing of configuration state in real time without performance penalty
candidates.action: Introduce a standardized, self-verifying handoff protocol that embeds observational metadata, provenance tags, and cryptographic hashes of configuration states directly into the instrument’s shared state — enabling recipients to instantly verify authenticity, detect tampering, and decide whether to reuse or reconfigure without relying on memory or trust in prior setups.
candidates.test: Simulate a handoff between two teams where one team modifies a configuration and the receiving team detects the change via mismatched hash — verify that the protocol flags the deviation and prevents unverified reuse.
candidates.alternative: Existing manual handoff with verbal or written notes, which are prone to misinterpretation, loss, or omission

candidates.title: Real-Time Configuration Optimization from Observations
candidates.uncertainty: Whether the AI model can generalize from sparse, noisy observational data to produce reliable, actionable configuration changes
candidates.action: Implement a real-time AI-driven configuration optimizer that uses incoming observational data (e.g., transient light curves) to dynamically suggest optimal instrument settings for the next task — without requiring full reconfiguration or prior setup knowledge.
candidates.test: Feed a simulated transient event into the optimizer and compare the suggested configuration to a known optimal setup — verify that the AI recommendation achieves at least 60% of the benchmark reward.
candidates.alternative: Manual configuration based on team experience or pre-defined templates

candidates.title: Instrument State Ledger with Immutable Provenance
candidates.uncertainty: Whether the ledger can be maintained without introducing latency or requiring additional hardware
candidates.action: Develop a shared instrument state ledger that logs every setup, modification, and handoff as a time-stamped, immutable record — accessible to all teams via a simple web interface — enabling transparent tracking and reducing coordination overhead.
candidates.test: Simulate two teams attempting to reuse a setup from a previous session — verify that the ledger reveals the exact configuration and last user, and that both teams can independently validate consistency.
candidates.alternative: No shared record; teams operate in isolation with no visibility into prior setups

candidates.title: Prefill-Based Proof of Instrument State
candidates.uncertainty: Whether the proof system can be implemented efficiently on low-end hardware or within the constraints of mobile instrument power budgets
candidates.action: Adopt a prefill-based proof system that generates cryptographic proofs of instrument state validity during initialization — allowing teams to verify that the instrument is in a known, trusted state before beginning a new task.
candidates.test: Run a prefill proof generation on a simulated instrument state and verify that the proof can be validated by a third party without requiring full re-execution of the setup.
candidates.alternative: No verification; teams assume initial state is correct

candidates.title: Modular Instrument Configuration Framework
candidates.uncertainty: Whether the physical interface design allows for reliable, quick module swapping without signal loss or calibration drift
candidates.action: Introduce a lightweight, modular configuration framework that allows teams to plug in and swap instrument modules (e.g., sensors, calibration units) via standardized interfaces — enabling rapid reconfiguration for different tasks without full disassembly.
candidates.test: Swap a sensor module in a simulated setup and verify that the new configuration is recognized and validated by the system within 30 seconds of connection.
candidates.alternative: Fixed, monolithic instrument setup with no modular flexibility
